Diagnostics attached to a registered tool, rather than a second execution engine. Every entry point uses the same recorder. Records live with the document and survive reopening. Capture is bounded and best effort: a full disk must not turn a successful edit into a reported failure.

### ToolPool { #toolpool-kt-toolpool }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ToolPool</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">directory</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">File</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">File</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">System</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">getProperty</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;user.home&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">&quot;.afield/tool-pool&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/ToolPool/#L169)

A local, cross-project library of box-authored tools. This stores source; it is not a tool registry. Curating is explicit. Loading an entry never runs it or imports the originating project's state. Run the returned source in a normal provider box to register its tools, then test in that project. Keep project-specific dependencies explicit in the provider source and entry description.

| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">summarySnapshot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CodeUseSummary</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/CodeUseTelemetryService/#L579) | Non-blocking counterpart to `summary` for hot polling paths such as the welcome screen. Returns the most recent computed summary immediately (even if a little stale), or a cheap "still gathering" placeholder if none has been computed yet, and kicks off a background recompute when the cache is stale. It never runs the full-table SQLite scans on the caller's thread, so it can't stall Netty request or workspace-search dispatcher threads — the cold first computeSummary() (which can take many seconds on a large database) no longer blocks the welcome response or, by dispatcher starvation, a document the user clicks right after. |

### CoroutineProfiles { #coroutineprofiling-kt-coroutineprofiles }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">CoroutineProfiles</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/CoroutineProfiling/#L87)

Box-owned continuation instrumentation, shared by Runloop and SimulationClock. A continuation's CPU/heap counters exclude its suspended lifetime. No timers or allocations on the disabled dispatch path. Export copies happen on request, not per resume. A process permits one capture at a time; document isolation also applies to stop/snapshot.

### FrameProfile { #frameprofile-kt-frameprofile }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FrameProfile</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">context</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CoroutineContext</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;Frame&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">targetFps</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">60.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">allocationKiB</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">512.0</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/FrameProfile/#L61)

Explicit frame boundaries for the existing Profiling panel. This object does not start a capture. Press Record in the panel, then call `beginFrame` once per application frame, on a stable thread. Intervals include time between boxes and waits; CPU/heap counters cover that thread only. Use `measure` for named inclusive stages. No counter reads or sample allocation while recording is off.

## PinnedConsole.kt { #pinnedconsole-kt }

A `LogSink` that pins chosen channels to a small, non-scrolling region at the *top* of the
terminal while every other log line scrolls normally below it.

The heavy lifting is a single ANSI scroll-region (DECSTBM): the top N rows are fenced off so
ordinary output can only scroll in the region beneath them, which means a plain `println` "just
works" — there is no per-frame render loop over application state. The header is repainted only
when a pinned value actually changes (coalesced by a single daemon tick), and the terminal size
is re-checked about once a second.

Selection is by channel tag: a log event whose comma-separated `channel` contains a pinned tag
(e.g. pinning `"audio"` matches `"info,audio"`) updates that tag's row instead of scrolling.
Configure via the `AFIELD_PIN_CHANNELS` env var (comma/space separated) and/or at runtime with
`pin`/`unpin`/`clear`.

Degrades cleanly: if stdout is not an interactive TTY, ANSI/cursor control is unavailable, or the
terminal is a legacy Windows console (Mordant reports `AnsiLevel.NONE`), pinning switches off and
every event — pinned or not — simply scrolls, with would-be-pinned lines tagged `pin` so they
stay visible. Set `AFIELD_PIN_DISABLE=1` to force this fallback.

Known limitation: raw `System.out.println`/stderr writes elsewhere in the app bypass this sink's
lock and can, very occasionally, interleave with a header repaint. They still scroll below the
header; the visual glitch is transient. Routing all app output through the dispatcher avoids it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/app/diagnostics/logging/PinnedConsole.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/logging/PinnedConsole/)

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">StatsHeatmap</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/logging/StatsHeatmap/#L16)

Colors the numeric tokens of a rolling-stats line (`"fps=61.2 upload=3.4MB net:102%"`) on a blue -> green -> yellow -> orange -> red heatmap keyed by whether each value rose or fell since the last line the same pinned channel emitted. A value identical to last time renders grey. History is kept per channel+key so unrelated metrics sharing a channel don't interfere.

## stdlib_diagnostics.kt { #stdlib-diagnostics-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/app/diagnostics/stdlib_diagnostics.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/stdlib_diagnostics/)

### NetStats { #netstats-kt-netstats }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">NetStats</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/server/NetStats/#L35)

Time-windowed WebSocket traffic stats for the front-end `/ws` channel, surfaced on the pinned "net" console row: `↑` = backend → front end, `↓` = front end → backend. Counters are bumped at the send choke point (`sendWithOutputBackPressure`) and the inbound frame loop; a 1s reporter emits per-second packet + KB rates — and only when there's traffic, so the pinned row dims then expires when the front end goes idle (see PinnedConsole's lifecycle).

### OutputBackPressureSnapshot { #server-kt-outputbackpressuresnapshot }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">OutputBackPressureSnapshot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pending</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">skipped</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">buffered</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maxPending</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">bufferSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/server/Server/#L977)

Tracks per-session back pressure for output messages. When the frontend is slow to acknowledge outputs, the pending count rises. Once it reaches `maxPending`, new outputs are held in a rolling buffer of size `bufferSize`. Messages that overflow the buffer are counted as truly skipped. When pressure eases, the buffered messages are flushed after the skip notification — they are never counted as skipped.

The note is shared with `tools/docs_notes.py`, which reads and writes this same file. Every top-level key that tool writes must be a property here, because `DocsAnnotationStore` rewrites the whole file from these data classes and `ignoreUnknownKeys` would silently drop anything else; `tools/test_docs_notes.py` (`KotlinSchemaTest`) fails when the two disagree. What only the tool understands lives inside `source`, which is kept verbatim.

## keyframeBrowsing.kt { #keyframebrowsing-kt }

The server half of the keyframe collection browser: one `/ws` raw channel, no new HTTP route.

The page itself is `keyframe_browser.html`, served by the static mount over
`src/commonMain/resources`, so nothing here widens Field's HTTP surface — which matters, because
every verbless `route(…) { handle { … } }` is an unauthenticated all-methods endpoint and there is
a census test counting them (`FieldApiCorsExposureTest`). A raw channel rides the socket the
client already has, the way the h2 explorer and the log stream do.

### What crosses the wire

Structure as JSON, presentation as HTML. The collection summary, the slot bands and the version
rows are typed payloads the page lays out itself; individual *values* come over as rendered HTML
from `.h`, because that is the whole point of reusing the value visualizers — a `Vector3f` arrives
with its axis widget already drawn, and a type that registers its own printer gets it for free.

### Read-only, deliberately

There is an `apply` op, because putting a saved look back is the reason
you were browsing. There is no edit op. Everything on disk is append-only by construction —
`saveKey` never overwrites a numbered version and an unreadable manifest is quarantined rather
than replaced — and an in-browser edit button would quietly break that. Getting a modified look
back out goes through `updateCode`, which emits pasteable Kotlin.

## upstreamcheck.kt { #upstreamcheck-kt }

Field is distributed as source: you clone it and you build it. So "is there an update" is not a
question about a version manifest and a zip, it is a question about your checkout and its remote
— and git already answers it. This asks, and reports. It never writes to the working tree; pulling
is yours to do, because only you know whether your checkout has work in it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/app/server/upstreamcheck.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/app/server/upstreamcheck/)

### Top-level functions { #upstreamcheck-kt-functions }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">checkUpstream</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">repoDir</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">File</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">File</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;.&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">remote</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;origin&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">timeoutSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">UpstreamStatus</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/server/upstreamcheck/#L81) | Asks `remote` what it has on this branch, and — only if that differs from HEAD — fetches so the new commits can be described. The cheap case costs one `git ls-remote`; nothing is fetched, and no ref is moved, when you are already up to date. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">updateCheckMessages</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">status</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">UpstreamStatus</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">maxNotices</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/server/upstreamcheck/#L192) | The lines to show for `status`, most important first. Notices come out whole and unabbreviated — a commit only carries one when someone decided every puller needs to read it. |

## PersonalReload.kt { #personalreload-kt }

Reloading [`PersonalLayer`](workspace.md#personallayer-kt-personallayer) at runtime, and coping with the objects the old one left behind.

`reloadPersonal` retires the live layer so the next engine compiles and runs against a freshly
built `afield-personal.jar`. The hard part is not the swap, it is that every already-evaluated
snippet holds classes from the layer that just died: an object made by gen-0 `kiwi.Solver` and an
object made by gen-1 `kiwi.Solver` are unrelated types, and mixing them produces the JVM's least
helpful error, `class kiwi.Solver cannot be cast to class kiwi.Solver`.

Two halves, a scan up front and a diagnosis at the point of failure:

 * `scanForStaleClasses` is a shallow, best-effort look at what an engine is holding, so the
   common case — a box with a personal object in a top-level `val` — gets caught and reset up
   front. It is deliberately incomplete (see its own docs) and makes no attempt to be otherwise.
 * `staleLayerDiagnosis` catches what the scan missed, at the moment it actually breaks, and says
   so in English. Because recovery is a one-click reset rather than a debugging session, the scan
   does not have to be good — it only has to keep most boxes from visibly hiccuping.

Neither half re-runs anything. A box whose engine was recycled is *marked* (`needsRerun`) and left
alone: Field does not execute user code that the user did not ask to execute, and a reload is not
an exception to that — re-running a box can open windows, start strands and hit the network.

## stdlib_collections.kt { #stdlib-collections-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

## stdlib_graph.kt { #stdlib-graph-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

## SafeSaveAtomicSmokeTest.kt { #safesaveatomicsmoketest-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/document/persistence/SafeSaveAtomicSmokeTest.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/document/persistence/SafeSaveAtomicSmokeTest/)

### SafeSaveAtomicSmokeTest { #safesaveatomicsmoketest-kt-safesaveatomicsmoketest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">SafeSaveAtomicSmokeTest</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/document/persistence/SafeSaveAtomicSmokeTest/#L58)

Smoke for `File.safeSave`'s `atomic = true` path — the fix for transient `operations.yaml` corruption (a reader catching a truncated/interleaved write). The operation-transcript writer (`OperationTranscript.checkpoint` and friends) now writes atomically: to a temp file in the same directory, then an atomic rename into place, so a concurrent reader (or another process sharing the workspace) only ever observes a complete file.

## props.kt { #props-kt }

The `prop` / `rootProp` macro pair — the typed, inheritable box-property slot.

`prop` and `rootProp` exist only as the declarations that make `prop<Int>(foo)` resolve; neither
is meant to run, and calling one throws `MacroRegistry.MacroNotExpandedException`. The real work
happens at expansion time in `macro_prop` and `macro_root_prop`, which are handed the type
argument and the name, and return an `Insert` that rewrites the call site to the bare name (or
`root.name`) and pushes two declarations into the box's preamble: a
`var Box.<name> by Inheritance<T>()`, a `val Once.<name> by Onceing<T>()` and a
`val Why.<name> by Whying()` (so `why.<name>` explains where the value comes from). All three generated
lines carry the trailing empty-comment marker that makes the preamble gather copy them down into
child boxes, and an import for `T` is added via `kotlinImportStatementFor`. `macro_root_prop`
differs only in targeting `this.root`, so the accessors land on the document root rather than
on the calling box.

## reactiveProps.kt { #reactiveprops-kt }

`propUp`, `propDown` and `propUpDown`: `prop` with re-execution attached.

All three declare the same typed, inherited slot `prop` does (a `var Box.<name>` in the preamble,
copied down into children), and read and write it the same way. What they add:

- **Up** — a read that finds no value anywhere up the graph runs the box that supplies it, then
  reads again. The supplier is the box that declared the property (or supplied it before), nearest
  first, and the run happens *inside* the read, so a chain of them unwinds in order.
- **Down** — a write that changes the value reruns, after the writing box's run has finished,
  every box that read the old value, in dependency order.

Declare it where the value is written (Down is decided by the writer's declaration, Up by the
reader's), and the declaration reaches the children as `prop`'s does. The scheduling is
`afield.runtime.lifecycle.ReactiveRuns`; what it did is in `ReactiveRuns.recentEvents()`.

## stdlib_properties.kt { #stdlib-properties-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

### Kits { #kits-kt-kits }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Kits</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/document/workspace/Kits/#L83)

Kits: one machine, many documents. A kit is what every document of one kind receives: the code of the boxes that play its roles (providers), the sources those boxes hold in other properties (a rule set, a recipe), and the asset files they read from the document's `files/` folder. It is a directory with a `kit.json` beside those files; `tools/field_kit.py` makes one from a document, rehashes it, installs it in a document, migrates a document to a newer revision and publishes it as a Welcome starting point. `public/docs/kits.md` is the user's page.

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">WelcomeDirCandidate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">filename</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">dir</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">File</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">metadataFile</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">File</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lastModifiedEpochMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sizeBytes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/document/workspace/dir/#L755)

A workspace document discovered by `welcomeDirCandidates`, described only by cheap `stat` metadata. Turning one into a [`WelcomeEntry`](workspace.md#dir-kt-welcomeentry) (box count + tags) requires parsing its metadata file, which `summarizeWelcomeCandidate` does lazily.

## stdlib_buffers.kt { #stdlib-buffers-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

## AaCompletionClient.kt { #aacompletionclient-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/completion/AaCompletionClient.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/AaCompletionClient/)

### AaCompletionClient { #aacompletionclient-kt-aacompletionclient }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">AaCompletionClient</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/AaCompletionClient/#L55)

Stage C client for the out-of-process K2 Analysis-API completion endpoint (`/complete` on the code-use semantic sidecar). Used only when `KotlinEngineConfig.activeCompletionBackend == AA`; `KotlinInterface2.complete` falls back to the K1 delegate whenever this returns null (no sidecar URL configured, HTTP/timeout failure, or the sidecar reports failure). The AA classpath deliberately stays out of the live runtime — this is a thin HTTP bridge, mirroring `CodeUseTelemetryService`.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">const</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">EXPECTED&#95;TYPE&#95;MATCH</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/AaCompletionClient/#L58) | `extraInfo` key marking a candidate whose type fits the type expected at the caret. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">const</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">DECLARED&#95;IN</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/AaCompletionClient/#L65) | Where a candidate is DECLARED (`kotlin.Any`, `afield.audio.synth`, `afield.graphics.render.ComputeMesh`). Read by `KotlinCompletionSupport.classifyMetadata` to categorise the row by its own declaration rather than by the receiver of the panel it appears in — see `DECLARATION_PROXIMITY`. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">const</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">DECLARATION&#95;PROXIMITY</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/AaCompletionClient/#L73) | `own` \| `supertype` \| `universal`: how close the declaration is to the receiver's own type. The client (`fieldSuggest.js`) turns it into a ranking term, so `ComputeMesh`'s own members sort above inherited ones, which sort above the names declared on `Any`/`T` that are true of everything (`also`, `apply`, `let`, and `T.onBeat`). |

Excludes `-jdk7`/`-jdk8` so JVM-only extensions don't leak into completions for code that runs in a JS head. Empty if none found (caller then skips AA). |

STAGE D live end-to-end: exercises the REAL KI2 → AA-sidecar completion chain in a running Field JVM. ## playlist.kt { #playlist-kt }

Playlist functionality for Field4

This module provides helpers for executing boxes in a defined order based on their `playlist` property.
Boxes with a `playlist` property (a Double) will be executed in order from lowest to highest value.
Between each `begin()` call, `executePlaylist` waits `pauseList` `frame()` calls (default 1).

User-facing dev doc: dev_docs/Playlist.md (a pointer stub); this KDoc is the source of truth.

## stdlib_execution.kt { #stdlib-execution-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">warmCompletion</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinInterface2/#L734) | Build the K1 completion delegate ahead of the first real completion. The bootstrap is a full intro+preamble compile (~seconds, longer the colder the JVM's K1 infra). If it instead fires lazily from inside a runloop-pumping wait it re-enters the K1 engine mid-compile and corrupts its analysis state (a "Rewrite at slice PACKAGE_TO_FILES" error). Warming here, on the non-reentrant runloop before any such wait, keeps every later completion light and safe. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">warmCompletionBackend</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">timeoutMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinInterface2/#L749) | Poll the AA sidecar with the real request shape until it actually serves, so the next completion is the one a user gets rather than the K1 fallback. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">warmCompletionAsync</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinInterface2/#L808) | Schedule `warmCompletion` on the main runloop (the same non-reentrant dispatcher `complete` uses) so the ~1s K1 bootstrap is paid ahead of the first real completion/error-suggestion request instead of stalling it. The `completionWarmInFlight` guard collapses the burst of edit events into a single scheduled warm; once warm for the current preamble, `warmCompletion` returns near-instantly (mutex + fingerprint check), and it re-bootstraps automatically when the preamble changes. |

Call this right after building an engine that will be bootstrapped asynchronously. Engines left un-armed (the default) never block — used directly in tests and ad-hoc snippet execution. No-op for engines without such a gate. |

Idempotent; a no-op for engines without such a gate. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">complete</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cursor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CompletionResult</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinScriptEngine/#L143) |  |

Doing it up front, on the same main-runloop dispatcher `complete` uses, gets the one heavy compile out of the way outside any re-entrant runloop pump, so later completions are light and single-threaded-safe. Idempotent; a no-op for engines with no lazy completion bootstrap. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">warmCompletionBackend</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">timeoutMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">120</span><span class="n">&#95;000</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinScriptEngine/#L165) | Build the *serving* completion backend, not just the fallback. |

Idempotent and self-de-duplicating (a no-op while a warm is already in flight, and cheap when already warm for the current preamble). AA is the out-of-process K2 Analysis-API sidecar (`AaCompletionClient` → `/complete`) and is the DEFAULT (Stage D cutover): it matches-or-beats K1 recall, passes all anti-goals, and adds named-arg completion. It only engages when a sidecar URL is configured (`afield.completion.sidecarUrl` / `AFIELD_CODE_USE_SEMANTIC_SIDECAR_URL`); otherwise, and on any timeout / error / empty result, it falls through to the compiler-grade K1 delegate, so AA is never worse than K1. Invaluable for debugging `rewrite {}`/`unquote {}`/builtin-macro output. Disable with `-Dafield.macros.logExpanded=false`. |

### WitherSmokeTest { #withersmoketest-kt-withersmoketest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">WitherSmokeTest</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/WitherSmokeTest/#L95)

Smoke for the experiment that wires the Wither compiler plugin (kyay10/wither) into the K2 REPL ([`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2)). Wither is a FIR + IR plugin: a call to `io.github.kyay10.wither.with(x)` turns `x` into an implicit receiver for the rest of the enclosing block, and its IR pass rewrites the receiver-less member accesses that follow.

### LedgerSlot { #lifecycleledger-kt-ledgerslot }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">LedgerSlot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">owner</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">key</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/LifecycleLedger/#L167)

### BoxRunScopes { #runscope-kt-boxrunscopes }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">BoxRunScopes</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">box</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/RunScope/#L357)

A box's [`RunScope`](workspace.md#runscope-kt-runscope)s: at most a few open per strand, the newest of which is the strand's current run, plus the one `parent` scope that no run supersedes. See [`RunScope`](workspace.md#runscope-kt-runscope) for when they open and close.

| --- | --- |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">begin</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">strand</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RunScope</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/RunScope/#L364) | Open a new scope for a run of `strand`; older scopes of the strand stay open until `supersede`. |

| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">parent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RunScope</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/RunScope/#L384) | The box-level scope no re-run supersedes. What it owns lasts until a stop, for `ReleasePolicy.RUNNING` things, or until the box retires, for everything else. A superseded run's `ReleasePolicy.KEYED` registrations move here, and `once.x { … }` computes with it current, so a value made once is not taken apart by the next run. |

Null for a deleted box, so a straggler registering after deletion owns nothing (the ledger still attributes it). |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">stopAll</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/RunScope/#L417) | Stop's part of the teardown: every scope, the parent included, releases what is `ReleasePolicy.RUNNING`. Returns how many run scopes there were. |

A coroutine scope with a manually stepped dispatcher. It creates no thread and registers no new box launcher. Use `withSimulationClock` inside ordinary `frames`; standard `launch` children inherit the box, source and parent job. `delay` and `withTimeout` then use simulation time. `advance` and `close` belong to the creating thread; dispatch and cancellation may enqueue from another thread.

## RewriteDsl.kt { #rewritedsl-kt }

The rule-authoring surface for the pattern-rewrite layer (see [`PatternRewrite`](workspace.md#patternrewrite-kt-patternrewrite)).

These declarations are *erased*: a `rewrite { … }` block is collected and deleted from the
source by `PatternRewrite.expand` **before** the K2 REPL ever compiles it, so none of these
functions is ever actually called at run time. They exist only so a rule authored in a live box
  - parses,
  - is importable (`import afield.runtime.macros.*`), and
  - reads sensibly (the names `rewrite` / `from` / `to` / `Expr` resolve to something).

The whole point (see [`PatternRewrite`](workspace.md#patternrewrite-kt-patternrewrite)) is that a rule body never needs to *type-check* — only
parse. PSI parsing runs no name resolution, so `from { max(x, y) }` parses into a valid tree even
though `max`, `x`, `y` resolve to nothing. If one of these functions is somehow reached at run
time it means expansion did not happen, which is a bug — hence the throw.

Surface:
```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
rewrite { x: Expr, y: Expr ->
    from { max(x, y) }
    to   { if (x >= y) x else y }
}
```
The lambda's value parameters (`x: Expr, y: Expr`) are the metavariable declarations: inside
`from`/`to`, a name reference is a hole iff its name is in that parameter set, and its declared
type names the [`MetaKind`](workspace.md#rewritedsl-kt-metakind). No `unquote`/`$`/`,` escape is needed — the known metavar set *is* the
escape.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/macros/RewriteDsl.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/macros/RewriteDsl/)

A reusable build stage. `inputKeys` selects only the authored inputs this stage consumes, and may name [`StudyBuildGate`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuildgate)s; `dependencies` names other stages whose current results must exist first, either in this runner or, written `dependsOn(runner, stage)`, in another runner of the same document. `recipeVersion` must change when the adapter or its relevant runtime changes. The runner does not infer code identity from a closure. `inputHelp` explains missing inputs without making the stage runnable or changing its fingerprint; a closed gate supplies its own explanation. `resultNotes` is a fast, pure presentation of a completed record's retained facts; it must not inspect mutable design state or change acceptance. It is shared by UI and agent tools and does not change build identity. Qualification gates belong in the build and input contracts. `build` runs on a worker and must use its captured context, not mutable live input.

What a study can say about a picture in numbers, and how it lays pictures out for a model to look at. Every study that draws — StackSL, RectSL, a stack.auto slot — measures and lays out its frames here, so a measurement means the same thing in all of them.

### StudyVerb { #livestudy-kt-studyverb }

## QualifiedSource.kt { #qualifiedsource-kt }

### Qualified sources: changing a rule without breaking what already works

A rule (a placement recipe, a fallback, a solver strategy) is a source that other builds consume.
A [`QualifiedSource`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedsource) keeps three things beside it and lets the rule change only when all three agree:

- the **rule**, a [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy) over a box property;
- the **fixtures**, a [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy) of retained real cases, each an exact input and the outcome the rule
  gave it ([`QualifiedFixture`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedfixture));
- a **replay** stage, a [`StudyBuilds`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuilds) runner that runs a candidate rule on every fixture and on a
  [`QualifiedControl`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcontrol), an input no correct rule can pass, which must fail.

A change starts as a *candidate*: a frozen record of the base it was made against, its source, the
fixtures, the dependencies and the checks ([`QualifiedCandidate`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcandidate)), named by the hash of all of them. The
replay compares each fixture's new outcome with the recorded one: the same, changed, or held (the rule
or its checks refused it). A candidate is admitted, and `apply` publishes it through
`SourceStudy.edit`, only when its replay is current, covers every fixture with the same outcome, the
control failed as it must, and nothing it depends on has changed.

The checks that judge a candidate are out of its reach ([`FrozenRegion`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-frozenregion)): files it may not edit, text
after a marker that must stay byte for byte, or a separate frozen copy. Only a person changes them, and
only a person changes a fixture's recorded outcome: `proposeRebaseline` draws each changed outcome with
an **Approve** button, and the press records who approved it and when. No tool approves.

`Box.qualifiedSource` makes one in a box and registers the agent tools `<name>.inspect`, `.candidate`,
`.test`, `.apply`, `.retainFixture` and `.proposeRebaseline`.

### QualifiedFixture { #qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedfixture }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">QualifiedFixture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">input</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">outcome</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/#L127)

A retained case: the exact `input` text and the `outcome` the rule gave it, which must survive a JSON round trip.

### QualifiedControl { #qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcontrol }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">QualifiedControl</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">input</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">messageContains</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/#L134)

An input no correct rule can pass, replayed with every candidate. Its replay must fail (the rule or its checks throw), with `messageContains` in the message when given. A control that passes means the checks are not running, so no candidate is admitted.

### FrozenRegion { #qualifiedsource-kt-frozenregion }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FrozenRegion</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/#L143)

Where a qualified source keeps its checks out of a candidate's reach. A candidate breaking any of its regions is refused before it is saved. What the regions freeze is recorded in the candidate as `QualifiedCandidate.checks` and handed to the replay as `QualifiedReplay.checks`.

## SourceStudy.kt { #sourcestudy-kt }

The language-neutral half of a live-code study: the part of "talking a function into existence"
that does not care what the language is.

A study holds one editable source — the text in a box that a person and a model are both working
on — and a durable, append-only history of the versions of it that passed a check. Every change
arrives as a *transaction*: the caller names the revision it read and a hash of the live source it
read, the candidate is checked by the language adapter, and only then is it written into the box,
with a compare-and-swap against the text that is there *now*. So a model preparing an edit while a
person types cannot overwrite the person, a candidate that fails its check changes nothing, and
every accepted version can be read back, compared and restored.

What the language adds is one function, [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy)'s `admit`: compile and check a candidate,
returning a value (whatever the language's tools need — a composition, a compiled shader report)
or throwing [`StudyRejection`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-studyrejection) with a message a person or a model can act on. The StackSL, RectSL,
stack.auto and function studies are all adapters over it; `FunctionStudy` predated it and kept a
private copy of the protocol until 2026-09-29, with the same file layout, so a revision directory
written before then still reads.

### On disk

`directory/<id>.<extension>` is a revision's source and `directory/<id>.json` its metadata (parent,
description, time, and whatever facts the adapter chose to keep). `directory/HEAD` names the checked
revision the box last held. An id is `r<n>-<first 12 hex of SHA-256(source)>`, so an id also
verifies its own file: a revision whose source was edited on disk refuses to load.

This is trusted local code, not a sandbox: `admit` runs whatever the adapter runs. Cancellation
(`cancel`) stops a pending publication, not a computation that never checks for it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/source/SourceStudy.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/SourceStudy/)

**Used in:** [Studies](../studies.md)

language's own rewriter, which keeps each number's spelling — as a new revision, with the usual guards: the knob indices refer to the live source the caller read, so a stale revision or hash is refused, and a value a word cannot hold is refused with the rewriter's reason. |

### StudyKnob { #studyknob-kt-studyknob }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StudyKnob</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">index</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">line</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">typed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">operand</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/ui/StudyKnob/#L43)

One number a person typed in a study's source — a *knob* — as everything language-neutral sees it: the fast model that names sliders (`KnobNames`), the keys a card saves (`StudyKeys`), a study's setNumbers tool.

### DocsUiDriver { #screenshot-kt-docsuidriver }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">DocsUiDriver</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pageProvider</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Page</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/screenshot/#L2784)

The single object a `drive` script touches. Every method marshals onto the Playwright dispatcher and blocks the calling (main runloop) thread for the result, so scripts never touch the thread-bound `Page` directly. `wait` sleeps on the *calling* thread, leaving the Playwright thread free to keep grabbing recorder frames.

## stdlib_output.kt { #stdlib-output-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).
